authorized_domains.description: List of domains authorized for OAuth redirects.
authorized_domains.rationale: Defines application-specific OAuth redirect domains; without knowing each team's legitimate domains, a generic platform policy cannot distinguish trusted from untrusted values.

autodelete_anonymous_users.description: Whether anonymous users will be auto-deleted after a period of 30 days
autodelete_anonymous_users.rationale: Controls the lifecycle of unlinked anonymous accounts, reducing the persistence of unused identities and their associated data.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Selects the Google Cloud project for this configuration but does not itself configure an authentication or authorization control.

blocking_functions.forward_inbound_crede.description: The user credentials to include in the JWT payload that is sent to the registered Blocking Functions.
Whether to pass the user's OAuth identity provider's access token.
blocking_functions.forward_inbound_crede.rationale: Forwards OAuth access tokens to a blocking function, expanding the set of systems that can access bearer credentials.

blocking_functions.forward_inbound_crede.description: Whether to pass the user's OIDC identity provider's ID token.
blocking_functions.forward_inbound_crede.rationale: Forwards OIDC identity tokens to a blocking function, exposing signed identity claims to that endpoint.

blocking_functions.forward_inbound_crede.description: Whether to pass the user's OAuth identity provider's refresh token.
blocking_functions.forward_inbound_crede.rationale: Forwards refresh tokens to a blocking function; refresh tokens can obtain new access tokens and require strict handling.

blocking_functions.triggers.description: Map of Trigger to event type. Key should be one of the supported event types: "beforeCreate", "beforeSignIn".

blocking_functions.triggers.event_type.description: The identifier for this object. Format specified above.
blocking_functions.triggers.event_type.rationale: Selects beforeCreate or beforeSignIn for team-authored blocking logic; both are platform-supported and the appropriate lifecycle event depends on that logic, so a universal constraint would not improve security.

blocking_functions.triggers.function_uri.description: HTTP URI trigger for the Cloud Function.
blocking_functions.triggers.function_uri.rationale: Identifies the endpoint that receives authentication-event requests and potentially forwarded credentials; it must be a trusted HTTPS function endpoint.

client.description: Options related to how clients making requests on behalf of a project should be configured.

client.permissions.description: Configuration related to restricting a user's ability to affect their account.

client.permissions.disabled_user_deletio.description: When true, end users cannot delete their account on the associated project through any of our API methods
client.permissions.disabled_user_deletio.rationale: Prevents end users from deleting their own accounts through Identity Platform APIs. A generic policy can require this to protect user records from unauthorized or accidental destructive loss.

client.permissions.disabled_user_signup.description: When true, end users cannot sign up for a new account on the associated project through any of our API methods
client.permissions.disabled_user_signup.rationale: Controls self-service account creation, which directly affects exposure to unauthorized registrations and abuse.

mfa.description: Options related to how clients making requests on behalf of a project should be configured.

mfa.enabled_providers.description: A list of usable second factors for this project. Possible values: ["PHONE_SMS"]
mfa.enabled_providers.rationale: Selects an MFA provider as part of the application's authentication architecture rather than enforcing a platform-wide security boundary. This field accepts only PHONE_SMS, so a generic policy cannot further constrain it.

mfa.state.description: Whether MultiFactor Authentication has been enabled for this project. Possible values: ["DISABLED", "ENABLED", "MANDATORY"]
mfa.state.rationale: Enables or mandates multi-factor authentication for the project, directly changing sign-in assurance.

mfa.provider_configs.description:
A list of usable second factors for this project along with their configurations.
This field does not support phone based MFA, for that use the 'enabledProviders' field.

mfa.provider_configs.state.description: Whether MultiFactor Authentication has been enabled for this project. Possible values: ["DISABLED", "ENABLED", "MANDATORY"]
mfa.provider_configs.state.rationale: Enables or disables configured multi-factor providers, changing which MFA protections users can use.

mfa.provider_configs.totp_provider_confi.description: TOTP MFA provider config for this project.
The allowed number of adjacent intervals that will be used for verification to avoid clock skew.
mfa.provider_configs.totp_provider_confi.rationale: Sets the TOTP clock-skew tolerance used to accommodate client clock drift. The appropriate window is an operational usability setting, not a generic platform security enforcement target.

monitoring.description: Configuration related to monitoring project activity.

monitoring.request_logging.description: Configuration for logging requests made to this project to Stackdriver Logging

monitoring.request_logging.enabled.description: Whether logging is enabled for this project or not.
monitoring.request_logging.enabled.rationale: Enables audit-relevant request logging for Identity Platform activity, supporting detection and investigation.

multi_tenant.allow_tenants.description: Whether this project can have tenants or not.
multi_tenant.allow_tenants.rationale: Enables the multi-tenant architecture feature. Whether the project should host tenants is a workload design choice with no universally safer enabled or disabled setting.

multi_tenant.default_tenant_location.description:
The default cloud parent org or folder that the tenant project should be created under.
The parent resource name should be in the format of "/", such as "folders/123" or "organizations/456".
If the value is not set, the tenant will be created under the same organization or folder as the agent project.
multi_tenant.default_tenant_location.rationale: References the organization or folder that owns tenant projects; the approved parent is environment-specific, and a generic policy cannot identify it without pinning a resource ID.

quota.sign_up_quota_config.description: Quota for the Signup endpoint, if overwritten. Signup quota is measured in sign ups per project per hour per IP. None of quota, startTime, or quotaDuration can be skipped.

quota.sign_up_quota_config.quota.description: A sign up APIs quota that customers can override temporarily. Value can be in between 1 and 1000.
quota.sign_up_quota_config.quota.rationale: Sets a temporary sign-up quota between 1 and 1000 requests per project, hour, and IP. The appropriate numeric limit depends on application demand, so a generic threshold would be arbitrary.

quota.sign_up_quota_config.quota_duratio.description: How long this quota will be active for. It is measurred in seconds, e.g., Example: "9.615s".
quota.sign_up_quota_config.quota_duratio.rationale: Sets the duration of a temporary sign-up quota override. The safe duration depends on the workload and operational incident, so a generic maximum would be arbitrary.

quota.sign_up_quota_config.start_time.description: When this quota will take affect.
quota.sign_up_quota_config.start_time.rationale: Schedules a temporary quota override; valid start times are deployment-specific and neither earlier nor later is universally more secure.

sign_in.description: Configuration related to local sign in methods.

sign_in.allow_duplicate_emails.description: Whether to allow more than one account to have the same email.
sign_in.allow_duplicate_emails.rationale: Allows multiple accounts to share an email address, weakening account uniqueness and increasing identity-confusion risk.

sign_in.anonymous.description: Configuration options related to authenticating an anonymous user.

sign_in.anonymous.enabled.description: Whether anonymous user auth is enabled for the project or not.
sign_in.anonymous.enabled.rationale: Enables unauthenticated anonymous identities, directly changing the application’s authentication attack surface.

sign_in.email.description: Configuration options related to authenticating a user by their email address.

sign_in.email.enabled.description: Whether email auth is enabled for the project or not.
sign_in.email.enabled.rationale: Enables an application sign-in method; whether email authentication is required depends on the application, and enabling or disabling it is not universally safer.

sign_in.email.password_required.description:
Whether a password is required for email auth or not. If true, both an email and
password must be provided to sign in. If false, a user may sign in via either
email/password or email link.
sign_in.email.password_required.rationale: Controls whether email sign-in requires a password. Requiring passwords enforces a stronger credential requirement than email-link-only authentication and reduces account-takeover exposure from compromised email links.

sign_in.phone_number.description: Configuration options related to authenticated a user by their phone number.

sign_in.phone_number.enabled.description: Whether phone number auth is enabled for the project or not.
sign_in.phone_number.enabled.rationale: Enables phone-number authentication; a policy may disable SMS sign-in to reduce SMS-pumping and SIM-swap exposure.

sign_in.phone_number.test_phone_numbers.description: A map of <test phone number, fake code> that can be used for phone auth testing.
sign_in.phone_number.test_phone_numbers.rationale: Defines test phone numbers and fake verification codes for phone-auth testing. Their use is environment-specific test configuration rather than a generic platform security control.

sms_region_config.description: Configures the regions where users are allowed to send verification SMS for the project or tenant. This is based on the calling code of the destination phone number.

sms_region_config.allow_by_default.description: A policy of allowing SMS to every region by default and adding disallowed regions to a disallow list.

sms_region_config.allow_by_default.disal.description: Two letter unicode region codes to disallow as defined by https://cldr.unicode.org/ The full list of these region codes is here: https://github.com/unicode-cldr/cldr-localenames-full/blob/master/main/en/territories.json
sms_region_config.allow_by_default.disal.rationale: Restricts the regions that may receive verification SMS when SMS delivery is otherwise allowed by default.

sms_region_config.allowlist_only.description: A policy of only allowing regions by explicitly adding them to an allowlist.

sms_region_config.allowlist_only.allowed.description: Two letter unicode region codes to allow as defined by https://cldr.unicode.org/ The full list of these region codes is here: https://github.com/unicode-cldr/cldr-localenames-full/blob/master/main/en/territories.json
sms_region_config.allowlist_only.allowed.rationale: Defines the exclusive allowlist of regions that may receive verification SMS, limiting SMS fraud and unwanted geographic exposure.
